original_value: AbstractSeveral researchers are trying to develop different computer‐aided diagnosis system for breast cancer employing machine learning (ML) methods. The inputs to these ML algorithms are labeled histopathological images which have complex visual patterns. So, it is difficult to identify quality features for cancer diagnosis. The pre‐trained Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have recently emerged as an unsupervised feature extractor. However, a limited investigation has been done for breast cancer recognition using histopathology images with CNN as a feature extractor. This work investigates ten different pre‐trained CNNs for extracting the features from breast cancer histopathology images. The breast cancer histopathological images are obtained from publicly available BreakHis dataset. The classification models for the different feature sets, which are obtained using different pre‐trained CNNs in consideration, are developed using a linear support vector machine. The proposed method outperforms the other state of art methods for cancer detection, which can be observed from the results obtained.

result.paraphrase: Abstract Several researchers have been working on developing computer-aided diagnosis systems for breast cancer using machine learning (ML) methods. These ML algorithms take labeled histopathological images as input, and the images contain complex visual patterns, making it difficult to extract quality features for cancer diagnosis. Recently, pre-trained Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have emerged as unsupervised feature extractors. However, only limited research has examined breast cancer recognition from histopathology images using CNNs as feature extractors. This study evaluates ten different pre-trained CNNs for feature extraction from breast cancer histopathology images. The images are taken from the publicly available BreakHis dataset. Classification models for the various feature sets produced by the selected pre-trained CNNs are built using a linear support vector machine. The proposed method outperforms other state-of-the-art cancer detection methods, as reflected in the results obtained.
